source.title: [Unmatched] Inarrêtable Excalibur !
source.related_product_date_not_article_date: 19 Février 2021 belongs to the Volume 1 product card, not the 2025 article

complete_normative_translation.french: Nos partenaires de Restoration Games viennent d’officialiser un changement de règles concernant le personnage du Roi Arthur.
complete_normative_translation.faithful_english: Our partners at Restoration Games have just made official a rule change concerning the character King Arthur.

complete_normative_translation.french: Pour comprendre ce changement, il faut prendre le temps de revenir sur la capacité d’Arthur, qui indique ceci :
complete_normative_translation.faithful_english: To understand this change, we need to take a moment to return to Arthur’s ability, which states the following:

complete_normative_translation.french: « Lorsque le Roi Arthur combat, il peut BOOSTER son attaque. Jouez la carte BOOST, face cachée, avec votre carte Attaque. Si votre adversaire annule les effets de votre carte Attaque, la carte BOOST est défaussée, sans effet. »
complete_normative_translation.faithful_english: When King Arthur fights, he may BOOST his attack. Play the BOOST card, face down, with your Attack card. If your opponent cancels the effects of your Attack card, the BOOST card is discarded without effect.

complete_normative_translation.french: Le changement de règle implique la carte Excalibur, une carte d’attaque de valeur 6. Auparavant, si la carte Excalibur, une fois boostée, était contrée par une Feinte, la Feinte avait pour effet de défausser la carte utilisée pour le Boost. Ce n’est plus le cas désormais, dans une modification officielle apportée par Restoration Games.
complete_normative_translation.faithful_english: The rule change involves Excalibur, an attack card with a value of 6. Previously, if the Excalibur card, once boosted, was countered by a Feint, the Feint caused the card used for the Boost to be discarded. This is no longer the case, under an official change made by Restoration Games.

complete_normative_translation.french: Cette règle prend donc immédiatement effet, aussi bien pour le jeu amical que pour les tournois :
complete_normative_translation.faithful_english: This rule therefore takes effect immediately, both for casual play and for tournaments:

complete_normative_translation.french: « Comme Excalibur n’a aucun effet imprimé sur sa carte, ses effets ne peuvent pas être annulés. Si Arthur utilise sa capacité pour BOOSTER Excalibur, la carte utilisée pour le BOOST n’est pas défaussée si l’adversaire annule les effets sur Excalibur. »
complete_normative_translation.faithful_english: Because Excalibur has no effect printed on its card, its effects cannot be canceled. If Arthur uses his ability to BOOST Excalibur, the card used for the BOOST is not discarded if the opponent cancels the effects on Excalibur.

translation_notes: French Feinte means the Feint card, not a generic cancellation category invented by the reviewer.
Jeu amical explicitly includes casual/friendly play; the change is not tournament-only.
The French article quotes combat (fights). The inspected original English character card says When King Arthur attacks; this review does not broaden the original ability to defense.

Not discarded is in the conditional context of the opponent canceling effects on Excalibur. Read with the stated prior-versus-new outcome, it removes cancellation’s discard-without-effect consequence; it does not confer post-combat retention.

authority_and_applicability.publisher_authority: Original supplied rulebook page 16 credits ©2019 Restoration Games, LLC and ©2020 IELLO for the translated version, names IELLO and its distribution contacts. This corroborates IELLO’s official involvement independently of the supplied provenance description.
authority_and_applicability.restoration_attribution: Normative paragraphs 1 and 4 explicitly attribute an official rule change to Restoration Games. This is publisher evidence, not a fan interpretation.
authority_and_applicability.original_volume_one: The article expressly discusses King Arthur, original ability text, Excalibur attack 6 and Feint, and links Unmatched – Combat de Légende – Volume 1 at https://iello.fr/jeux/unmatched/. Inspected original English character and action-card images match those facts.
authority_and_applicability.scope: Effective immediately for both casual play and tournaments, per paragraph 5; publication date is 11 August 2025. The article contains no limitation to another set or a new card edition.

supersession.prior_exact_ruling: That's not how it's intended. If you Feint a boosted Excalibur, it cancels the boost effect.
supersession.identity_corroboration: Allowed author API identifies Justin Jacobson, designer ID 4083 and Restoration Games publisher ID 34846. Original rulebook page 16 credits Justin D. Jacobson for game restoration.
supersession.reason: The 2025 publisher explicitly calls the prior Feint-discard result formerly applicable and says it is no longer the case under an official Restoration Games change. The later explicit change supersedes the older intention for play under current errata.

source_derived_rules.cancellation_result: Against textless Excalibur, Feint does not cancel the King Arthur ability BOOST and does not cause its card to be discarded without effect; the BOOST contributes to the attack value.
source_derived_rules.reason: Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, explicitly stated in normative paragraph 6 and visually confirmed on original action-card image.

card_facts.excalibur: Attack 6, no printed effect text, top row fourth card in original action-card image
card_facts.feint: Versatile 2; IMMEDIATELY: Cancel all effects on your opponent’s card.; bottom row first three cards
card_facts.ability: Original English character image: play the BOOST card face down along with the attack; original cancellation clause discards the BOOST without effect.

general_discard_rule.source: extracted/unmatched-rules.txt, original page 12, Step 3: Resolve Combat
general_discard_rule.exact_text: Finally, all played cards are placed in their respective discard piles.
general_discard_rule.supporting_general_rule: Original page 10: All cards, once played and resolved, should be placed in the discard pile.
general_discard_rule.application: Arthur plays the BOOST card along with Excalibur. Cancellation does not prematurely discard it without effect; after combat resolves, the played BOOST card and other played cards go to their respective discard piles under the unchanged general rule.
general_discard_rule.no_hand_return_or_retention_exception: Neither the publisher article nor the original general discard rule instructs returning the BOOST to hand or retaining it after combat.

numerical_example.conditions: Excalibur base 6, an ability BOOST card with printed BOOST value 3 (for example Noble Sacrifice in the inspected original card image), opposed by Feint defense 2, with no other modifiers or damage prevention
numerical_example.math_source: Original rulebook page 12 instructs subtracting the defense card value from the attack card value.

residual_gaps: The Restoration Games original 2025 announcement itself was not supplied or separately inspected; the direct official IELLO article explicitly relays its official rule change. This does not leave the publisher-authority gap open.

The article does not spell out ordinary end-of-combat disposal in its not-discarded sentence; the supplied original general played-card discard rule supplies that step. No retention or hand-return rule is inferred.
The human/coordinator choice between printed-original-only scope and current official errata scope remains pending; this review makes no source-scope preference decision.
